page: The Microsoft Azure D4als_v6 is a virtual machine instance from the Dalv6 family, powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. This instance features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with multithreading enabled. It is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The instance operates on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, does not include local storage, and has no GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core compute capabilities, with the stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core performance and memory-bound operations show clear limitations. The Passmark memory score is in the bottom 10%, and memory bandwidth benchmarks for both cached and uncached read-only operations are in the bottom 25%. This bottleneck impacts memory-intensive tasks, as seen in the weak performance for software compilation and database operations.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D4als_v6 offers a budget-friendly entry point for compute-focused workloads that do not require large memory footprints or local storage. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent processing power, making it suitable for single-threaded tasks, text processing, static web serving, and lightweight containerized applications. It is less suitable for memory-heavy databases, large-scale software compilation, or complex multi-threaded decompression tasks.
